 by

 Nov 4, 2026 
 Listen 
 Listen 
 The NFL never disappoints, does it? Week 8 is in the books, and what a week it was. We no longer have an undefeated team, and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers won despite Baker Mayfield attempting just three passes without a completion, something we haven’t seen in over 50 years. With only two teams on bye, let’s get into the FantasyPros Fantasy Points Allowed tool and a few other resources to identify good and bad fantasy football matchups for Week 9.

 Fantasy Points Allowed: Best & Worst Matchups (Week 9) 
 Week 9 Quarterback Fantasy Football Matchups 
 Good Matchup: Malik Willis (QB – MIA) vs. Detroit Lions 
 Malik Willis is a viable streaming option, though the matchup may not be as favorable as it was earlier this season. 
 The Lions have allowed the most fantasy points to quarterbacks, but the secondary got a much-needed boost with Brian Branch returning from injury. Still, Willis’ rushing floor adds fantasy value in what remains an overall favorable matchup. 
 Willis ranks third among quarterbacks in rushing yards per game with 32.1, and he’s taking shots downfield with a 9.1 average depth of target (aDOT). 
 Among 30 qualifying quarterbacks, Willis ranks 14th in deep pass attempts and fourth in deep-pass percentage, per the Fantasy Points Data Suite. 
 According to Sharp Football Analysis, the Lions’ defense allows explosive plays at the league’s highest rate (8%). If Willis can connect on a couple of long bombs, he could finish as a back-end QB1 this week. 
 Bad Matchup: Kirk Cousins (QB – LV) @ San Francisco 49ers 
 It’s been a magical ride, with Kirk Cousins sitting as the QB5 in fantasy points per game. He’s played better than most expected, but how sustainable is this offense? 
 Brock Bowers leads the Raiders in receptions, but running back Ashton Jeanty is right behind him. That kind of passing game may be tough to sustain as a QB1. 
 The 49ers have been much stronger against the run, but they still rank 11th in passing yards allowed, giving up 223.9 per game. The Raiders also haven’t run the ball well, with Jeanty averaging just 3.12 yards per carry, and he could still be in the Kubiak doghouse. 
 If San Francisco contains the run, it could put Cousins in obvious passing situations, making it harder to move the chains. Despite the strong play, his three-game streak of top-12 finishes is in jeopardy. 
 I would rather pivot to Malik Willis, Bo Nix or Sam Darnold , who all have better matchups this week. 
 Week 9 Running Back Fantasy Football Matchups 
 Good Matchup: Jonah Coleman (RB – DEN) @ Carolina Panthers 
 Raise your hand if you held Jonah Coleman this long. It paid off last week when he took full advantage of his opportunity with RJ Harvey on injured reserve (IR) against a good Kansas City run defense. 
 Coleman was on the field for nearly 68% of the snaps, outcarrying Dobbins 11-7 while running 17 routes on 34 dropbacks, per the Fantasy Points Data Suite. He sparked this offense both on the ground and in the receiving game, finishing RB12 for the week. 
 The rookie back gets a much juicier matchup against Carolina. The Panthers have given up the second-most fantasy points to running backs, 4.73 yards per carry and 10 rushing touchdowns. 
 With the increased workload and involvement in the passing game, Coleman is a solid RB2 with RB1 upside. 
 Bad Matchup: D’Andre Swift (RB – CHI) vs. Tampa Bay Buccaneers 
 You can’t fade D’Andre Swift after his three-touchdown performance against the Seahawks on Monday night. If you have him, you’re starting him, but don’t expect another top-five finish. 
 Seattle was a tough opponent, and his touchdown hat trick overshadowed his inefficiency on the ground. He carried the ball 27 times for 69 yards. Tampa Bay has actually been even better against the run, allowing only 80 rushing yards per game. 
 The Buccaneers have yet to allow a single running back to reach the century mark, and they give up the second-fewest fantasy points to the position. Swift remains a must-start, but treat him more as an RB2 this week. 
 Week 9 Wide Receiver Fantasy Football Matchups 
 Good Matchup: Jordan Addison (WR – MIN) vs. Buffalo Bills 
 Although Justin Jefferson commands plenty of defensive attention, Jordan Addison remains a risky FLEX option. Still, he leads the team in air-yard share, ranks second in target share and has an elite 91.2% route rate. 
 Buffalo allows 8.17 yards per target and 37.1 fantasy points per game to wide receivers. 
 The Vikings’ offense will see a fairly even split between man and zone coverage. Among 81 qualifying wide receivers, Addison ranks eighth in overall separation score, according to the Fantasy Points Data Suite, and gets open at a high rate against both man and zone defenses. 
 Addison has some volatility behind Jefferson, but the plus matchup gives him enough upside to be a roll-of-the-dice FLEX option. 
 Bad Matchup: Michael Wilson (WR – ARI) @ Seattle Seahawks 
 As mentioned last week, Michael Wilson is a plug-and-play option in a favorable matchup, but he’s also an easy fade when it turns difficult. Seattle allows the fewest fantasy points to wide receivers, making this about as tough as it gets. 
 Jacoby Brissett is now on the sideline after getting benched, and Gardner Minshew Mania is officially underway. To Wilson’s credit, they looked good together in the comeback win against Dallas. 
 Wilson also showed his toughness by playing through two broken ribs, but the injury adds another layer of risk. With this offense still uncertain, Wilson is best left on your bench this week. 
 Week 9 Tight End Fantasy Football Matchups 
 Good Matchup: Harold Fannin Jr. (TE – CLE) @ New Orleans Saints 
 Harold Fannin Jr. has caught 21 passes for 245 receiving yards over the last two games. He’s been on an absolute tear, and this matchup gives him a good chance to keep it rolling. 
 The Saints give up the sixth-most fantasy points to tight ends. Fannin has averaged 4.14 yards per route run (YPRR) against single-high coverage across the last two weeks, well above his 1.91 YPRR for the season, per the Fantasy Points Data Suite. 
 The recent production comes in a small sample, but it’s encouraging against a Saints defense that runs single-high at the second-highest rate in the league and has allowed the fourth-most fantasy points per dropback. 
 Start Fannin with confidence as a TE1. 
 Bad Matchup: Dalton Kincaid (TE – BUF) @ Minnesota Vikings 
 Dalton Kincaid’s season has been up and down, and now he faces his toughest matchup yet. The Vikings have allowed the fewest fantasy points to tight ends and haven’t given up a touchdown to the position. 
 The usage has been solid. Josh Allen has spread the ball around, but Kincaid still leads the team in targets. He is averaging 3.8 catches and 57.3 receiving yards per game. 
 Still, Kincaid has had three games with three or fewer targets. Against a defense this tough on tight ends, his inconsistent volume makes him difficult to trust. 
 Kincaid is a sit for me this week. Consider streaming Brenton Strange , Mike Gesicki or Greg Dulcich instead.
